KEY MESSAGE 1...The nor'easter will retrograde back towards New 
Jersey over the weekend before finally departing on Tuesday. This 
will bring periods of additonal rainfall and strong winds to the 
region.

Broad high pressure remains centered over eastern Canada and extends
back into the Great Lakes. While the high will weaken and lift into
northern portions of the Province of Quebec, it will still be strong 
enough to create a tight pressure gradient between it and the low 
off the New Jersey coast. While we'll see a little bit of lull in 
the winds overnight, an increase is once again expected tomorrow. 

We will keep the High Wind Warnings and Wind Advisories in place, 
but extend them into Sunday. We have posted new Wind Advisories for 
our remaining zones to the north and west. Given that trees still 
have their leaves, the combination of these winds and heavy rain 
will result in downed trees and also power lines. Property damage 
cannot be ruled at the coast where the winds are highest. 

With the track closer to the coast, the higher PoPs that were 
introduced early this morning will remain in place. PoPs are pretty 
much in the 80 to 100 percent range across the whole area tonight 
and Sunday. Event rainfall totals will be in the 1 to 2 inch range 
along the I-95 corridor and points north and west with as much as 3 
inches over much of eastern New Jersey. Locally heavier amounts are 
possible. This will be over a 48 to 60 hour timeframe, so widespread 
freshwater flooding is not anticipated at this time. That said, the 
Millstone River at Griggstown is now expected to crest above flood 
stage. This is our only forecast point above flood stage. It goes 
without saying that and freshwater runoff will exacerbate the 
flooding along the coast. It simply will not be able to drain. We 
cannot rule out a few embedded thunderstorms.

KEY MESSAGE 2...More Moderate to Minor tidal flooding expected 
for tonight and Sunday. Highest levels water levels will trend
less as the storm begins to weaken later Sunday. 

A slow moving Nor'easter offshore will remain into Sunday and
begin to weaken. Although this current/most recent high tide will
be/has been the most impactful, we're not out of the woods yet 
along the coast and back bays. Additional flooding will occur 
over the next several high tides. There are no changes with the 
headlines right now. While widespread major flooding is not 
expected going forward, widespread moderate is. 

For Delaware Bay communities, north/northeast winds will keep 
pushing water to the west side of the Bay and onto the Delaware 
coast. This will increase the water levels for those communities.
The Coastal Flood Warning remains in effect until 2 AM Sunday 
for Kent and Sussex, DE. Moderate Flood levels are forecasted for 
Cumberland and Salem, NJ as well as New Castle, DE, so the Warning 
will remain in place across these areas. 

For the tidal Delaware River, we expect the minor tidal flooding
will take place both with the upcoming high tide this afternoon
and again early Sunday morning. The strong North to Northeast
flow is for the most part keeping the water levels in check for
those areas. 

As mentioned above,the north to northeast winds will limit the 
tidal flooding threat for the Chesapeake Bay. Some spotty minor 
tidal flooding is anticipated at Claiborne around dawn Sunday, 
but nothing higher than that at this time. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...Dangerous rip currents and high surf are expected at 
the Jersey Shore and Delaware Beaches through Sunday. Additional 
beach and dune erosion can be expected.

A nor'easter is bringing strong north to northeast winds and 
high seas for our marine zones. Breaking waves within the surf 
zone of 6 to 12 feet will occur through Sunday. Dangerous rip 
currents will accompany the high surf, making it extremely 
dangerous to enter the water at any time through Sunday. The 
high surf and strong winds are resulting in areas of beach 
erosion across the Jersey Shore and Delaware Beaches. Across 
some locales, large breaking waves and run- up are also eroding 
dunes.

The High Risk for life threatening rip currents remains in 
effect through Sunday for all beaches. A High Surf Advisory is 
in effect for all beaches through Sunday as well.

The risk for dangerous rip currents will begin to decrease on 
Monday as winds shift offshore and wave heights begin to 
decrease. For now have opted for a MODERATE risk for all shore 
points.
